"name": "Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere"}], "description": "The `pull_request_target` event is designed to run trusted workflows from the
base branch with access to repository secrets. When such a workflow calls a
local reusable workflow via `uses: ./.gitea/workflows/...`, Gitea resolves the
reusable workflow file from the fork's HEAD commit instead of the base branch
commit.

Because `pull_request_target` intentionally bypasses the fork-PR approval gate
and the secret-access gate, attacker-controlled reusable workflow code can run
with access to repository and organization secrets.

## Details

Gitea already recognizes that `pull_request_target` must use the base branch:
in `services/actions/context.go`, `github.sha` and `github.ref` are overridden
to the base commit for `pull_request_target` events.

```go
// context.go
if run.TriggerEvent == actions_module.GithubEventPullRequestTarget {
    ref = git.BranchPrefix + pullPayload.PullRequest.Base.Ref
    sha = pullPayload.PullRequest.Base.Sha // overridden to base
}
```

The same override is not applied to the commit used to resolve reusable
workflow sources. In `services/actions/notifier_helper.go`, `handleWorkflows`
uses a single `commit` variable (the PR HEAD commit) for every detected
workflow, including `pull_request_target` workflows. The HEAD SHA is stored as
`WorkflowCommitSHA`/`WorkflowSourceCommitSHA` on the run and propagated to the
run jobs.

When `loadReusableWorkflowSource` in `services/actions/reusable_workflow.go`
resolves a local (`./` or `$/`) reusable workflow, it reads the file from
`WorkflowSourceCommitSHA` — the fork's HEAD commit — rather than the base
branch commit.

The top-level calling workflow is correctly detected from the base commit
(`baseCommit` in `notifier_helper.go`), so only the reusable workflow resolves
from HEAD. This inconsistency indicates an implementation bug rather than an
intended design choice. On GitHub, local reusable workflows referenced from a
`pull_request_target` workflow resolve from the base branch.

## Impact

A repository with a `pull_request_target` workflow that calls a local reusable
workflow can have attacker-supplied reusable workflow code executed with access
to repository and organization secrets by anyone able to open a pull request
from a fork.

Secret masking in workflow logs is a display-layer filter only and does not
prevent exfiltration, since executing code can transmit or transform secret
values arbitrarily.

## Affected configurations

- Gitea Actions enabled, and
- a workflow triggered by `pull_request_target` that calls a local reusable
  workflow via `uses: ./...` (or the `$/` same-repo form).

## Remediation

Resolve local reusable workflow sources for `pull_request_target` runs from the
base branch commit, consistent with the existing `github.sha`/`github.ref`
override, so `WorkflowSourceCommitSHA` points at the base commit rather than the
fork HEAD.

Until a fixed release is applied, operators can mitigate exposure by avoiding
`pull_request_target` workflows that call local reusable workflows, or by
scoping/limiting secrets available to fork pull requests.

## Credit

Chakradhar Chirumamilla — https://www.linkedin.com/in/chakradhar-chirumamilla/
